messages:
Jordan: FYI — customer 'FinLogic' reporting decrypt failures after our latest security push. They say it's blocking production. urgent ETA on patch?

Maria: Ticket #INC-2198 created and added FinLogic account rep. Customer wants immediate mitigation and a written plan.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2198 - hsm-decrypt-failure - priority: P0

Shreya: Can you paste repro steps and the exact error? I'll triage and engage infra.

Jordan: Repro steps from customer:
```
# curl repro
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/kms/decrypt \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -d '{"ciphertext":"BASE64...","key_id":"finlogic/prod/key1","alg":"RSA-OAEP"}'
```
Error:
```
2026-03-15T09:21:03Z ERROR kms.decrypt failed: key_unwrap: RSA_padding_check_PKCS1_type_2:incorrect
2026-03-15T09:21:03Z WARN audit: missing entry for unwrap attempt id=4f3b
```

Alex: Initial glance — unwrap failures coming from HSM vendor changes after a security patch. Some units are rejecting PKCS1 v1.5/compat profiles depending on key metadata. Might be CVE-related. Pulling vendor advisory now.

Shreya: Is this isolated to FinLogic or multiple customers? region-limited?

Jordan: So far FinLogic + one EU partner. Both using Dedicated with HSM-backed keys (firmware v2.1.3).

Maria: Customer demands rollback of the security change or a safe workaround. Also flagged billing/SLA: they're on committed capacity and threatening to divert traffic if not fixed.

Alex: Short-term options:
- Rotate affected keys to a compatibility profile and rewrap ciphertexts (requires coord).
- Enable software unwrap fallback for a subset of non-PCI keys (increases attack surface, must be audited).
Neither is ideal for cardholder data.

security-team: Marking this CVE-sensitive. No PoC disclosure externally. Sec team contacting vendor for timeline; do not share raw logs outside internal channels.

Jordan: Customer asked for reproable PoC. We should provide sanitized steps only. Who owns rollback plan/approval?

Shreya: I'll open a canary rollback to previous HSM firmware on 2 nodes in prod for validation. Canary rollback needs approval from security & infra; estimate ~30m/node and brief key availability windows.

Alex: Vendor hotfix estimate (prelim): 24-48h for a hotfix; full signed firmware build in ~72h. We can do temporary firmware rollback in ~2-3 hours if security approves and HSM vendor supports it.

Maria: I'll draft the customer communication with 3 options (canary rollback, non-PCI key rotation, temporary software unwrap for non-PCI). Sending now. :mailbox_with_mail:

ops-bot: Runbook link created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hsm_wrap_failure (internal)

Jordan: Proposed immediate steps for FinLogic:
1) Provide sanitized repro to security-team (no binary PoC)
2) Ask customer to opt-in to non-PCI server-side key rotation (we can rewrap server-side)
3) Offer canary rollback window for 2 nodes; if successful escalate to broader rollback
4) If rotation chosen, expect 5–10s extra decrypt latency during rewrap windows

Alex: Server-side rewrap flow (sketch):
```
GET /v1/keys/finlogic/prod/key1 -> key-meta
TRY HSM unwrap -> if success, wrap into new key_id 'finlogic/prod/key1-compat'
IF HSM unwrap fails AND key is non-PCI -> use software unwrap fallback with enhanced audit and sec approval
```
All software unwraps will be logged with audit markers and flagged for later secure review.

security-team: Approved: canary rollback on 2 nodes only.
No software fallback for PCI-regulated keys. Any operation that exposes plaintext outside HSM must have written customer consent.

Jordan: FinLogic confirmed non-PCI keys can be rotated. They requested an ETA today within business hours.

Shreya: Scheduling canary: 2026-03-16T02:00Z. Oncall: @alex @security-team standby. I'll post results and metrics (success rate, unwrap errors, audit logs).

Alex: Preparing scripts and extra audit hooks. Will monitor unwrap error rate and latency.

Maria: Customer message sent with options and request for consent. Keeping legal & compliance in loop. :lock:

Jordan: Thanks team. Keep channel locked to Redwood staff only — CVE-sensitive. Update here after canary. :thumbsup:
